description: Issue #787's crash path again, this time OVER-APPLIED, so it lands on a diagnostic instead of a value: `define forward … return 55 … end` then `print (fd 1 2)`. Before the fix this crashed the host with the same raw `TypeError` the sibling fixture `heritage-reporter-alias-reaches-canonical-user-procedure` documents — the arity check in `runProcedureBody` never ran, because the undefined lookup blew up on the line before it. Two things are asserted here that the clean-run sibling cannot: that a reporter-position alias call reaches the user procedure's ARITY guard at all, and that the resulting `ol-too-many-inputs` carries the CANONICAL `params.callable` `"forward"` — byte-identical to what `print (forward 1 2)` reports, never the surface `"fd"`. That is the rule #670 (`operation`), #733 (`callable`), and #741 (`keyword`) each established one param at a time and this saga has now had to re-close five times: diagnostic identity is `code` plus structured `params` (`spec/error-model.md:235-238`), Heritage is "alternate spellings only, no new semantics" (`spec/conformance.md:146`), so a param whose value changed with the spelling would itself be the observable semantic difference the profile forbids. Only the prose `message` may echo the learner's own word — and here even it says `forward`, because the message is rendered from the resolved callable rather than from the span. The `source_span` still covers the two columns of `fd` the learner wrote, so canonicalizing the param did not canonicalize the span. `"execute": true` because `execute()` runs `parse()` only and never `check()`, which is precisely why the static arity rule cannot cover this path.
